storyBody.heading: From Check-In to Vertical Transit
paragraphs: In late January 2013, a guest entered a Los Angeles hotel and moved through routine guest procedures: registration, room assignment, and normal elevator travel as part of a private trip plan. The sequence is important because the first stage is ordinary infrastructure, not mystery, with normal records and ordinary building systems.

That ordinary opening forms the record boundary. A documented start in civic routine is what allows the later sequence to stay traceable as a specific incident instead of drifting into anonymous folklore.

storyBody.heading: Missing Alert and Institutional Response
paragraphs: When the guest stopped responding to private contacts, family members reported her missing and police opened a public missing-person response. This converted a private absence into an evidentiary chain with official channels, timestamps, and a defined duty of care process.
The cause-action split here is clear: non-response triggered external intervention, and that intervention made the incident verifiable as a formal case sequence.

storyBody.heading: Elevator Visual Chain and Threshold Logic
paragraphs: Police released hallway and elevator camera records showing unusual elevator movement before police recovered the person. The key sequence in public reporting was not that the footage proved motive, but that the footage defined the last public movement envelope: entrances, exits, and repeated level transitions in a closed vertical space.

In legend terms, that is a threshold object: a machine that carries people between spaces, where each pause at a floor is a crossing point. The ambiguity was not supernatural in itself; it was procedural uncertainty about what happened between documented points.

storyBody.heading: Search Operations and Roof Route Control
paragraphs: Investigators and building responders expanded the sequence from camera review to physical search across shared and restricted service areas. Roof access and structural layout became a practical focus because it was where official teams could either complete or close possible movement paths.

The operational effect was a narrowing of the unknown. Instead of indefinite conjecture, attention narrowed to specific routes, floor controls, and the gap between the last known recorded motion and where she was found.

storyBody.heading: Rooftop Recovery and Forensic Sequencing
paragraphs: On February 19, 2013, emergency water-system work on the hotel’s rooftop led to the discovery of the missing person’s body in an elevated tank. The case then moved from disappearance to recovery and then to official medical review.
That phase is where the event ended as one bounded forensic sequence. The core documented chain is now complete: routine entry, missing report, camera review, search operations, and recovery.
